  - main:
    - text: CLASS 12 · MATRICES AND DETERMINANTS
    - heading "Determinants and Geometric Area" [level=1]
    - text: See how a 2×2 matrix transforms the unit square into a parallelogram. The determinant gives the signed area (orientation + size). Interactive Lab
    - link "← School lessons":
      - /url: /lessons/school
    - article:
      - text: MATRIX A (ADJUSTABLE) A =
      - spinbutton "matrix entry row 1 column 1": "3"
      - spinbutton "matrix entry row 1 column 2": "1"
      - spinbutton "matrix entry row 2 column 1": "1"
      - spinbutton "matrix entry row 2 column 2": "2"
      - complementary:
        - button "⚄ Random"
        - button "↳ Identity I"
        - button "Swap columns"
        - button "Transpose Aᵀ"
    - article:
      - text: ◇ det(A)
      - strong: 3 · 2 − 1 · 1 = 5
      - emphasis: = 5
    - article:
      - text: ◇ Orientation
      - strong: ⟳ Positive (Counterclockwise)
    - article:
      - text: ◇ Area
      - strong: "|det(A)| · 1 = 5"
      - emphasis: square units
    - article:
      - heading "BEFORE TRANSFORMATION (UNIT SQUARE)" [level=2]
      - img: "-2 -1 0 1 2 3 4 e₁=(1,0) e₂=(0,1)"
      - text: → e₁=(1,0) → e₂=(0,1) Unit square area = 1
    - text: A →
    - article:
      - heading "AFTER TRANSFORMATION BY A" [level=2]
      - img: "-2 -1 0 1 2 3 4 u1=(3, 1) u2=(1, 2)"
      - text: → u₁=(3,1) → u₂=(1,2) Parallelogram area = 5
    - article:
      - heading "DETERMINANT (SIGNED AREA)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: det(A)=ad−bc
      - paragraph: = 3·2 − 1·1
      - paragraph: = 5
      - strong: Positive ⇒ Counterclockwise orientation
    - article:
      - heading "AREA CONNECTIONS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: • Parallelogram area = |det(A)| = 5
      - paragraph: • Triangle area = ½|det(A)| = 2.5
    - article:
      - heading "WHAT IF det(A) CHANGES SIGN?" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Negative determinant is clockwise orientation. Area magnitude stays the same.
      - strong: ⟳ Positive (Counterclockwise)
      - strong: ⟳ Negative (Clockwise)
    - article:
      - heading "WHEN det(A) = 0 (COLLAPSE)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The vectors become linearly dependent. The parallelogram collapses into a line segment. Area = 0.
    - text: ●────────● (0,0) (2,0)
    - article:
      - text: Example A = [[2,4],[1,2]]
      - strong: det(A)=2·2−4·1=0
    - complementary: "▲ IMPORTANT: AREA USES ABSOLUTE DETERMINANT Geometric area is always non-negative. Use |det(A)|, not det(A), to compute area."
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE (CORRECT)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: 1) det(A) = 3·2 − 1·1 = 5
      - paragraph: "2) Orientation: det(A) > 0 ⇒ Positive (Counterclockwise)"
      - paragraph: 3) Parallelogram area = |det(A)| = 5
      - paragraph: 4) Triangle area = 2.5
      - paragraph: 5) Transformed vectors are the columns of A.
    - article:
      - heading "CHECK (OPTIONAL)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A = [3 1; 1 2]
      - paragraph: Aᵀ = [3 1; 1 2]
      - text: det(A)=5, |det(A)|=5
    - article:
      - heading "VERIFICATION" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "Column product check:"
      - paragraph: Ae₁ = (3,1)
      - paragraph: Ae₂ = (1,2)
      - text: "Determinant cross-check: 5 ✓"
